decisions.rationale: BrowserQueryOptionsBase adds supportedDialogKinds?: string[]. This browser transport option does not apply: Local and cloud use the Node SDK query API, whose dialog options are already configured independently.

resumeSseStream(query): boolean is a new Browser SDK export. Neither the Local adapter nor the standalone cloud worker uses the Browser SDK or its SSE query transport; no resume integration is needed for this Node SDK update.

suspendSseStream(query): boolean is a new Browser SDK export. Local and cloud queries run through the Node SDK; browser SSE suspension is outside the integration and is not a substitute for Zeros turn cancellation.

core.d.ts re-exports BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES and LEGACY_TOOL_NAME_ALIASES from ./sdk.js. The desktop contract imports both runtime entry points and verifies that their inventories agree; desktop and standalone worker tests validate the names Zeros actually handles.

ArtifactOutput adds optional owned flags to five artifact/asset output variants. Zeros keeps the existing bounded tool-content/resource-link handling and does not map this provider flag to Zeros workspace ownership or new artifact UI.

CronCreateOutput nextFireAt is consumed by both Node translators as the authoritative due time, including the scheduler offset. Local one-shot waiting snapshots and matched lifecycle wake-up notices prefer it to the existing cron estimate; ScheduleWakeup keeps scheduledFor. Root UserPromptSubmit sources distinguish dynamic loops from scheduled tasks. The cloud hook emits status only, without Stop-hook tracking or idle-policy changes.

BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES supplies the runtime inventory for contract tests over the actual desktop adapters, renderer title matchers and standalone cloud worker. Every special-cased name must be canonical, an SDK legacy alias or an explicitly documented retired compatibility name. The existing edit-tool set and canonical Agent name also use the tuple type; inventory membership alone never enables a product feature.

LEGACY_TOOL_NAME_ALIASES supplies subagent aliases to both Node translators. Matching remains anchored and case-insensitive; native names, persisted identities and current output stay unchanged. Contract tests require each legacy spelling to have its canonical target covered by the same surface, and an injected SDK alias proves that routing follows the export. Mixed-provider renderer fallbacks retain their existing behavior under source assertions without importing the Node SDK into the renderer.

McpSdkServerConfig adds tools?: McpServerToolPolicy[] for host-registered SDK servers. Policy interpretation remains in the Node SDK/CLI. Zeros adds no per-tool policy override and preserves existing MCP configuration and approval behavior in both placements.

Query.reloadPlugins options add addPlugins?: SdkPluginConfig[]. Zeros lists and refreshes Claude plugins but has no flow that enables one, so the additive option has no caller. Existing no-argument reloads remain valid; adoption is deferred until Zeros can enable plugins.

SDKControlElicitationRequest.property_order is not applicable to host adoption: the SDK does not forward it to onElicitation. Its documented order already follows JavaScript object-key order, including index-like names first, which the existing requestedSchema.properties iteration preserves. Local forms and the cloud cancellation response need no change.

Local and cloud summary refreshes share validation and forward known stable category IDs plus MCP tool/instruction server estimates through optional wire fields. The renderer uses IDs ahead of name fallbacks, joins only unambiguous CLI-normalized server identities, reconciles rounded estimates to the native totals, and exposes the server breakdown with keyboard disclosures. Missing detail keeps legacy rows; Skills remain visible and deferred tools stay outside the window. The credential-free bundled CLI confirms summary mode supplies the data. Optional custom-agent and skill plugin/path metadata is not presented.

SDKControlGetUsageResponse extends both behavior summaries with max_effort, workflow, always_on_context and large_tool_results, plus optional recommendations and fix objects. This usage API is experimental and remains unused; Zeros does not expose or depend on it in Local or cloud.

SDKControlInitializeRequest.sdkMcpServerConfigs entries add tools?: McpServerToolPolicy[]. The Node wrapper owns this control-handshake serialization. Zeros uses query() rather than authoring initialize frames and supplies no new SDK-server permission policy.

SDKControlMcpCallRequest adds result_not_for_model?: boolean, a capability-gated app-only result mode. Zeros does not issue these direct MCP control calls or enable this mode; existing agent tool results and their transcript handling are unchanged.

SDKControlMcpStatusRequest adds liveReply?: boolean for upstream CCR/Remote Control live event streams. Zeros Local and cloud run the Node SDK with stdio, not that upstream cloud transport; existing mcpServerStatus() calls keep the wrapper's normal response behavior.

SDKControlReloadPluginsRequest adds wire field add_plugins?: SdkPluginConfig[], corresponding to Query.reloadPlugins({ addPlugins }). Zeros has no flow that enables a plugin and therefore no caller for additive loading. Adoption is deferred until that flow exists; existing no-argument reloads keep their behavior.

SandboxSettingsSchema adds optional allowNestedUserNamespaces. The CLI defaults it to false and owns native settings validation. Zeros supplies no override for this setting; existing Local permissions and cloud VM isolation remain unchanged.

Settings adds attributionProject, attributionProjectPolicy.default, sshHostCommands and sandbox.allowNestedUserNamespaces. These remain native SDK/CLI settings; Zeros exposes none of these fields as a preference, telemetry mapping, SSH command surface or sandbox override, and retains each placement's existing settings sources.

The five new methods (thread/sample, thread/sample/cancel, thread/readState/update, thread/items/read and feedback/save) are typed protocol availability only. Zeros sends none of them; sampling suggestions and diagnostic ZIP export are explicitly deferred.
thread/readState/changed is available through the generic typed native subscription. It has no canonical transcript, unread UI or worker behavior; existing notification handling remains unchanged.

The aggregate v2 schema follows the individual reviewed subjects: new client methods stay generated-only, read-state notification subscription stays generic, and image-generation changes are handled by the desktop and standalone worker mappers. This wrapper adds no separate product capability.

Managed storage defaults describe Codex Desktop workspace creation, not filesystem grants. Zeros does not call configRequirements/read or adopt provider project-parent or projectless-workspace roots; Local and cloud workspace ownership remains Zeros-owned.

The optional WebSocket request ID affects the native environment/add connection and reconnect. Zeros does not call that generated-only route or use Codex environments as workspace placement identities.

preModelRequest and postModelRequest use the existing hook/started and hook/completed lifecycle. Both mappers retain the bounded event-name string and stable hook identity without a new special-case UI or config surface.

Desktop and worker retain optional bounded inputImages path/SHA-256 metadata in tool output. The renderer presents deduplicated literal source paths as Edited from file pills through the chat's existing Local/cloud Files navigation. Sources never change the generated target, title or count; old records omit the row and hidden rows cannot warm or open sources.

PreModelRequest and PostModelRequest managed hook matchers are executed and enforced by the native runtime. Zeros does not author managed hook requirements; its existing generic hook notifications remain the transcript boundary.

The added toolListMeta is opaque first-page catalog metadata. Zeros keeps the existing server/tool inventory and OAuth status mapping and does not expose or interpret this new metadata as credentials, tools or product state.

sci and sci_plus remain opaque account plan strings. The account reader and quota projection already accept strings; no plan-name allowlist controls execution, model selection or cloud organization authorization.

New voice names, optional v3 voice inventory and voiceSessionId are available in generated bindings only. Zeros has no native realtime-session UI. The shipped codex-resources/voice runtime is retained in desktop and worker packages; excluding it is a deferred packaging decision.

Optional encrypted_content and status fields on raw Responses items stay within Codex persistence and model transport. Zeros uses normalized ThreadItem notifications; it neither decodes the ciphertext nor projects it as transcript text.

experimentalPredictionMode and experimentalDisablePredictionMcp are not set by the existing explicit thread/fork path. Cache-preserving prediction forks and sample suggestions are not enabled; normal fork model, workspace and history behavior stays unchanged.

Image generation accepts attachment-store fileId or fallback inline result. Desktop and worker preserve usable inline previews; otherwise completion schedules one nonblocking savedPath read of a bounded, stable regular PNG/JPEG/WebP file without symlink traversal. Canonical image bytes survive worker history reload. Missing, unsafe or undecodable previews show Image saved by Codex; optional source pills stay separate. A fileId is never a URL, and late content enrichment cannot change status or cross Stop/turn replacement.

The experimental bounded persisted-item read route is not called. Zeros continues to load its own durable transcript and existing native history paths; exposing item-by-ID retrieval is not part of this runtime upgrade.
